variants.verbatim: sphinx-rfm clone: app-based tests and real builds fail at startup (ExtensionError/VersionRequirementError) because the venv's sphinxcontrib.applehelp/devhelp/htmlhelp/serializinghtml/qthelp and alabaster are too new for the checkout — sphinx/application.py unconditionally loads them as builtin extensions. Seen on both the old 3.0.x state (aca3f825f) and the current 4.x-era state (232dbe41c, Oct 2021, ~4.3-dev). Workaround: prepend a stubs dir to PYTHONPATH containing a regular `sphinxcontrib` package with stub modules whose `setup(app)` returns `{"version": "stub", "parallel_read_safe": True}`, plus an `alabaster` stub package that appends the real site-packages alabaster dir to its `__path__` (theme.conf needs `alabaster.support`) and provides `get_path()`. Working stubs: `/tmp/sphinx_type_hint_links/stubs` (recreate if /tmp cleared). Usage: `PYTHONPATH=/tmp/sphinx_type_hint_links/stubs python -m pytest ...`. For manual builds use `html_theme = 'basic'`; intersphinx accepts a local `objects.inv` path (hand-craft v2 format: text header + zlib-compressed entries) to avoid network. (The formerly noted pre-existing failure tests/test_util_inspect.py::test_signature_annotations passes at 232dbe41c.)
variants.prose: sphinx-rfm clone: app-based tests and real documentation builds fail at startup with ExtensionError or VersionRequirementError because the virtualenv's sphinxcontrib helper packages (applehelp, devhelp, htmlhelp, serializinghtml, qthelp) and the alabaster theme are newer than the checkout supports, and sphinx's application module loads all of them unconditionally as builtin extensions. Seen on both the old 3.0.x state (aca3f825f) and the 4.x-era state (232dbe41c, Oct 2021, about 4.3-dev). A workaround is known to work: shadow the too-new packages with stub versions kept in a scratch directory that Python's import path is made to search first when running the test suite. Each stub module only needs a setup function that reports a stub version and declares itself safe for parallel reads, and the alabaster stub must additionally forward to the real installed package's theme files and expose its path helper, because the theme configuration still reads alabaster's support module. For manual builds, switching the HTML theme to the plain builtin one sidesteps the problem entirely, and intersphinx can be pointed at a hand-made local inventory file instead of fetching over the network. The previously noted pre-existing inspect-signature test failure no longer occurs on the 4.x-era state.
variants.abstract: General recipe for era-pinned checkouts whose virtualenv has moved past them: when startup dies with VersionRequirementError/ExtensionError (or similar) because installed extension packages are too new for old code that loads them unconditionally, do not try to upgrade or downgrade the venv — shadow the packages. (1) Read the startup error to list which packages the checkout refuses. (2) Build a stubs tree: `mkdir -p <stubs>/<package>` with a minimal `__init__.py` per refused module whose `setup(app)` returns `{"version": "stub", "parallel_read_safe": True}`. (3) Put the stubs first on the import path for test runs: `PYTHONPATH=<stubs> python -m pytest <tests>`. (4) If a shadowed package must still serve real data files (themes, templates), have its stub append the real site-packages directory to `__path__` and re-export the helpers the host code calls. (5) For manual builds, prefer the tool's plainest builtin theme or backend so optional packages never load, and point network-fetching steps (such as intersphinx inventories) at local files. Applies to any repository pinned to an old era inside a newer environment, not only this one.
variants.placebo: black, flake8, mypy, and isort are not installed in the xarray development venv. Code should follow black's formatting conventions with 88-column line length (black standard). Type checking and linting require manual verification or installing these tools separately. | dask is not installed in the xarray test environment. Dask-chunked parametrizations are skipped (~97 tests) during pytest runs on xarray/tests/. This is expected and does not indicate a test failure. | Running xarray tests with NumPy ≥1.22 generates a pre-existing DeprecationWarning in Variable.quantile about nanpercentile's interpolation= argument. This is safe to ignore generally, but the test_quantile_interpolation_deprecated test asserts on it—avoid running with `-W ignore::DeprecationWarning` as it will suppress the warning and cause the test to fail. | The full test_dataset.py and test_dataarray.py test suite modules run in approximately 5 seconds on the xarray repo. When running tests during development, there is no need to use -k filters to subset tests—the full suite is fast enough to run without subsetting.
